First read /tmp/htb/brief_common.md and follow it exactly.

TASK: implement the Entire session reader, so Viva can compare what a human asked for with what the agent did. This is what makes Viva different from diff-only quiz tools.

Context: packages/engine/src/sources/session.ts has a stub `entireSource` that returns null. The Entire CLI 0.13.1 is installed at /Users/marcus/.local/bin/entire and logged in, and it's enabled on this repo. Commits with agent work get an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, and `entire checkpoint explain <id>` shows the prompt, transcript and files. Run `entire agent-help` and read the docs at https://docs.entire.com/llms.txt. I could not confirm how to script checkpoint output, so find out, rather than assuming a JSON flag exists. Checkpoints can also be read as git refs under refs/entire/checkpoints or the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch. See https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md.

Do this:
1. Implement `entireSource` so that, given a repo and head commit, it finds the checkpoint for the commits being pushed and returns intent (the human's prompts) and transcript. Handle ranges: a push can hold several commits and sessions. Make it work end to end on a real checkpoint from this repo. If no real checkpoint with an agent transcript exists yet, say so plainly in the PR.
2. Fall back cleanly to null when Entire is absent, the commit has no checkpoint, or the data is malformed. A missing or broken Entire must never break a review or a push.
3. Bound the size: transcripts can be enormous, and context per review is capped by `maxInputTokens` in config. Keep human prompts first, then the agent reasoning most relevant to changed files, and truncate deliberately. Treat all of it as untrusted, using the existing `untrusted()` wrapper.
4. Respect the data boundary: transcript text must never reach the ledger, logs or traces.
5. Add unit tests using fixture data, so CI passes without Entire installed.

Update the known-gaps section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. You are on branch entire/session-reader. End commits with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>.

------
# Working on Viva

Instructions for coding agents and humans.

## Rules

- Run `pnpm check` before calling work finished, and report the result honestly.
- `packages/contracts` is the contract. Change it first, then update `fixtures/mock` so the frontend keeps working.
- Deterministic steps run before any model call. Add a precheck before adding a prompt.
- All model access goes through `LlmProvider`. Output must be parsed by a zod schema.
- Wrap repository and session text with `untrusted()`. It is data, never instructions.
- Diffs, transcripts and model output never enter the ledger or logs. Only scores and hashes do.
- Hard gates (`skippable: false`) must never become configurable or skippable.
- Fail open: a Viva crash must never stop someone pushing.
- Use a one-question check file in `checks/` rather than growing an existing prompt.
- Never commit keys. Use `.env`.
- Keep everything working on Windows: no shell-only scripts, and use `node:path`.
- Add a test for every bug fixed. Add an eval case for every new prompt behaviour.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts`: shared zod schemas
- `packages/engine`: the review pipeline, ledger and fog
- `apps/vivad`: local daemon and `viva` CLI
- `apps/web`: The Fog and the exam room
- `checks`: one markdown file per check
- `evals`: tests for prompts
- `fixtures/mock`: sample data for the UI

Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` before changing the pipeline.

/** What the human asked for, and what the agent reasoned, for a change. */
export interface SessionContext {
  source: "entire" | "request" | "none";
  intent: string | null;
  transcript: string | null;
}

export interface SessionSource {
  load(repoPath: string, head: string): Promise<SessionContext | null>;
}

/**
 * TODO(marcus): read the Entire-Checkpoint trailer on `head`, then fetch the
 * checkpoint. Confirm how `entire checkpoint explain` can be scripted first.
 */
export const entireSource: SessionSource = {
  async load() {
    return null;
  },
};

export async function resolveSession(
  source: SessionSource,
  repoPath: string,
  head: string,
  requestIntent?: string,
): Promise<SessionContext> {
  const session = await source.load(repoPath, head);
  if (session) return session;
  if (requestIntent) return { source: "request", intent: requestIntent, transcript: null };
  return { source: "none", intent: null, transcript: null };
}

# Architecture

Viva reviews the human, not the code. It deliberately follows the same design as Mabel, the PR engine G-Research described in their workshop, so that it feels familiar to engineers who run this kind of system.

| Mabel | Viva |
|---|---|
| Reviews whether the code is right | Reviews whether a person understands it |
| GitHub PR, Kafka, review service, Kubernetes job, Python harness | `git push`, pre-push hook, local daemon, engine |
| One question per check, in markdown | Same, in `checks/` |
| Verdicts: reject, defer, approve, endorse | Same |
| Aggregate: worst wins | Same, across graded answers |
| Deterministic checks before any LLM call | Same, so many pushes cost no tokens |
| Prompt injection scan defers | Same, and it is a hard gate |
| Some gates can't be disabled by config | `skippable: false` gates |
| Changes to its own config need a human | `.viva/config.json` and `.viva/checks/` are protected |
| Findings stay in the job. Only verdict, counts and status leave | Diffs and transcripts stay in the review. Only scores and hashes reach the ledger |
| Evals: tests for prompts, graded on finding bugs and not flagging clean changes | `evals/`, same grading |

## The review

```
git push
  -> pre-push hook -> vivad
  -> collect the diff and session context
  -> deterministic prechecks       docs only, too large, protected paths
  -> injection scan                match: defer, cannot be skipped
  -> checks, in parallel           one question each, schema-enforced
  -> risk ranking                  plain arithmetic, no model
  -> plan up to 3 questions
  -> exam                          voice or typed
  -> grade                         separate model, transcript and rubric only
  -> aggregate, worst wins
  -> ledger -> verdict -> hook
```

Each step stops the review if it can decide, so the cheapest step wins.

## Design rules

- **Fail open.** If the daemon is down, the push goes through with a warning. Reliability beats coverage, as in HRT's Blobby talk.
- **Budget per review.** `MeteredProvider` counts tokens and enforces a cap, so a bug can't burn the credits.
- **Separate grader.** The examiner converses, while the grader only sees the transcript and rubric, so accent and fluency can't affect a score.
- **Ledger in git notes.** It needs no server, travels with the repo, and leaves your branch alone. `refs/notes/viva` has to be pushed explicitly to share it.
- **Understanding expires.** Mastery halves every 14 days, and halves again when the code changes.

## Known gaps

- The Entire adapter and entire-graph are stubs. The session source returns nothing, and blast radius uses `git grep`.
- `pnpm evals` still uses the mock provider, so check quality on real diffs is unmeasured.
- The fog is per file, with blast radius at 0. Symbol-level needs entire-graph.
- Reviews are held in memory, so restarting the daemon loses them.
- Ledger notes aren't pushed automatically yet.
- The pipeline has only run on macOS. CI covers Windows, but nobody has tried the hook on Windows yet.

## Open problems

From G-Research's list, and worth raising with their judges:

- Callers in other repos that nobody declared.
- Asking questions of confidential design docs without leaking them.
- Determining the risk of a repo with this system enabled.
------
# Tasks

Ordered by priority. Pick one, branch, and open a PR. Each should stay small enough to review.

## Backend (Marcus)

- [ ] **Real model:** run `GeminiProvider` on real diffs and fix it. Then run `pnpm evals` with it.
- [ ] **Entire session source:** read the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer and load the prompts and transcript.
- [ ] **Silent decisions:** tune `checks/silent-decision.md` until it separates requested from unrequested changes on real sessions. Question quality decides whether this project works.
- [ ] **entire-graph:** use it for blast radius, and measure tokens with and without it.
- [ ] **Brain:** save spoken reasoning as project memory.
- [ ] **Streaming:** push review events to the UI over SSE.
- [ ] **Persistence:** keep reviews across restarts.
- [ ] **Ledger sync:** push and fetch `refs/notes/viva`.
- [ ] **Skip with debt:** expose it in the CLI and record it in the ledger.

## The Fog (Kay)

- [ ] Replace the placeholder with the real map and fog visual.
- [ ] Animate fog rolling in and clearing.
- [ ] Add teammate colours and the bus-factor view.
- [ ] Set the visual identity.

## Exam room (Sophina)

- [ ] Add the ElevenLabs agent. Feed it the plan and capture the transcript.
- [ ] Add `highlight_code` and show the code being discussed.
- [ ] Add the live transcript, typed fallback and verdict screen.
- [ ] Add skip with debt.

## Demo and evidence (Pedro)

- [ ] Confirm the JetBrains criteria and how Air must be used.
- [ ] Build the demo repo with one seeded silent bug.
- [ ] Add 10-15 real agent diffs to `evals/cases`, including clean refactors.
- [ ] Run the comprehension study with hackers on Sunday morning.
- [ ] Write the pitch, opening on the problem and closing with "pick any file and quiz any of us".
- [ ] Finish the Devpost submission and `docs/AI_DISCLOSURE.md`.

## Stretch

- [ ] Memory layer for "is this the right direction?" questions, suggested in the team doc for G-Research.
- [ ] JetBrains tool window showing the map.
- [ ] Trail comment with the verdict.
- [ ] Tiger Data debt-over-time chart.

----
entire checkpoint explain — Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo gh/owner/name
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo et/project/repo
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
                 (positional, --checkpoint, or --commit) and a checkpoint that
                 has been pushed. A commit SHA is resolved to its checkpoint
                 by that repo's Entire API, so prefixes cannot be used here.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied,
                   including its subagent task records under "tasks".
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --task           With --transcript, stream a subagent's stored transcript
                   instead, selected by tool_use_id or agent_id (as listed
                   under "tasks" in --json).
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint. This is the only
                part of this command that writes: it stores the summary on the
                checkpoint and spends tokens with the configured summary
                provider. Every other mode only reads.
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

When to use this:
Reading a checkpoint is free: with no flags, or with --json, --full,
--transcript or --raw-transcript, this only reads and is safe to run
whenever you need the context. --generate is the exception — it writes a
summary onto the checkpoint and spends tokens with the summary provider,
so pass it only when the user asked for a summary. To see what subagents
did, read "tasks" in --json, then stream one subagent's transcript with
--transcript --task <tool_use_id>.
